articles.title: Chelsea go top of WSL as Sandy Baltimore bullet sees off Manchester City
articles.summary: Pragmatic, resolute and gutsy. Sonia Bompastor showed her ruthless side and delivered a tactical masterclass as Chelsea earned a 1-0 win over Manchester City and leapfrogged them at the top of the Women’s Super League.
body: Sandy Baltimore’s stunning strike in added time at the end of the first half was the difference, as the west London side nullified the threat of a team that had scored in each of their preceding 21 games in all competitions, delivering their first loss of the campaign.

The task for City got even tougher when goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita received a straight red for clattering into Alyssa Thompson, but despite their numerical disadvantage it was end to end right up until the final whistle.

Momentum was with City after their 5-0 defeat of West Ham the preceding weekend and a 4-1 win against Inter in the Champions League on Tuesday night. They were able to welcome the injured duo Vivianne Miedema and Beth Mead back to the bench to bolster their matchday squad.

articles.title: Tenerife boss says Owono's 12-match ban 'feels light'
articles.summary: Tenerife boss Alvaro Cervera reacts to goalkeeper Jesus Owono's 12-match ban as the club prepare for their first game since the death of Jesus de Miguel.
body: Tenerife manager Alvaro Cervera says that goalkeeper Jesus Owono's 12-match ban "might feel light" but he accepts that the regulations do not "specifically account for what happened".
FC Andorra's Owono, 25, was sent off after colliding with Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel during the closing stages of the Spanish second-tier match between their two respective sides on 2 November.
De Miguel died the following day aged 30, and a disciplinary committee from the Spanish football federation confirmed Owono's suspension on Friday.
It was the maximum punishment that he could have received as the disciplinary committee could only consider the offence on the pitch and not "the tragic outcome of the incident".

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino asked the US to believe in his project. Did he believe in it himself?
articles.summary: The coach’s tenure with the USMNT brought a whiplash of highs and lows. He met some goals but also left many with the impression he never truly bought in. It did not take US men’s national team coach Mauricio Pochettino very long to take his first big swing.
body: He’d just taken the reins of the program after a disastrous performance at the 2024 Copa América cost his predecessor his job, with the first home World Cup in three decades looming on the horizon. The federation introduced him in New York City, on the 24th floor of a building overlooking the Hudson River. In short order, he was asked about the culture surrounding the program. In his answer, he invoked the four-time World Cup champion US women.
“We need to believe that we can win,” Pochettino said that day in September 2024. “That we can win not only a game: We can win the World Cup.”

It is the type of belief that feels almost alien to observers of the US men, the type of statement that American fans yearn to hear so badly from a coach yet also roll their eyes at. For years, fans of men’s soccer in the US have been desperate to taste glory, and for years they have developed an inferiority complex spurred along not only by results but by international perception. Even in the present day, with American players playing in Europe at the very highest level, the idea that the US could win a men’s World Cup feels borderline preposterous.

articles.summary: Loss in Singapore marred by unruly end to friendly. Argentina beaten 2-1 by Uruguay in Buenos Aires. Raphinha was sent off as Brazil crashed to a 3-2 defeat to Japan in their international friendly in Singapore.
body: Japan went 2-0 up inside 20 minutes through Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura. Vinicius Junior reduced the deficit in the 33rd minute and scored again to drag them level on 75 minutes, before Sakamoto’s controversial late winner.

Argentina ’s post-Messi era began with a 2-1 defeat at home against Uruguay in Buenos Aires. The loss marked the World Cup finalists’ first match since Lionel Messi’s international retirement in early October.

Leonardo Balerdi opened the scoring with an own goal in the 48th minute, before Maximiliano Araújo doubled Uruguay’s lead in the 53rd minute under their new coach, Diego Forlán. Julián Álvarez pulled one back for the hosts in the 73rd minute.
This clásico rioplatense on Friday also kicked off a new chapter for Argentina under Lionel Scaloni, who extended his contract through 2030 this week.

articles.title: Meetmebythesea gives McManus a first Paddy Power Gold Cup
articles.summary: Ben Pauling’s Meetmebythesea showed his liking for Cheltenham once more and delivered owner JP McManus with his first victory in the prestigious Paddy Power Gold Cup.
body: Sent off the heavily backed 2-1 favourite on his first run since winning as a novice at the Festival in March, he put in some tremendous leaps on the way round for Harry Cobden.

Blueking d'Oroux, having his first run for Dan Skelton, looked the biggest danger after long-time leader Quebecois faded but Meetmebythesea powered away up the hill to win by two and a half lengths to give Cobden a second big victory in two days in the McManus colours.
Pauling said: "Harry wanted to ride him forward because not many are coming from behind today and he jumped brilliantly and travelled so well.
"I was a little worried turning for home that Dan's horse was going so well but he showed a lot of guts and then won well. Jumping the last he had plenty left and he has so much pace for a big horse.

articles.title: Chacarra reveals plan for 'dream' win over McIlroy and 'Dubai double'
articles.summary: Eugenio Chacarra is eyeing more than just holding off Rory McIlroy to Race to Dubai victory at the DP World Tour Championship, following a strong finish to his third round.
body: Chacarra entered the week with a 533.93-point lead over McIlroy in the season-long standings, having won three times this year, only to lose ground with rounds of 72 and 71 over the first two days at Jumeirah Golf Estates.

McIlroy temporarily moved above Chacarra into projected top spot, as he chases a record-equalling eighth Order of Merit title, with the world No 2 also briefly jumping to the top of the leaderboard before stuttering to a third-round 72.

Chacarra made nine birdies - including four in his last six holes - to post a four-under 68 and join McIlroy on five under, four strokes behind leader Tyrrell Hatton, but the Spaniard remains hopeful of challenging for tournament victory and 'Dubai double'.
"A lot of good and a lot of bad," Chacarra said about his performance. It has been a grind and I've been fighting. I've played all year on DP World Tour and I've played a lot.

articles.title: Immense Wales pull off sensational first victory over All Blacks since 1953
articles.summary: Wales pulled off one of rugby's biggest shocks of recent times as immense defence saw them to a 35-28 Nations Championship victory over New Zealand - a first vs the All Blacks since 1953.
body: Wales' victory was built on the foundation of some of their best 40 minutes of rugby for some time in the first half, leading 14-0 and 21-7 after tries from scrum-half Tomos Williams, hooker Dewi Lake and tighthead Archie Griffin.

A decision to keep playing deep in the first half instead of kicking out proved costly, though, allowing New Zealand to level the contest by the break via tries from scrum-half Cortez Ratima, No 8 Wallace Sititi and wing Fehi Fineanganofo - the last score coming three minutes into dead time at the end of the first half.
Yet, Wales emerged and flew into a big lead again at the start of the second half, scoring converted tries through centre Eddie James and wing Louis Rees-Zammit for a 35-21 advantage.

Peter Lakai quickly narrowed the deficit to seven with an All Blacks try, and the remainder of the contest was played out almost exclusively inside the Wales 22, only for the home side to repel wave after wave of attack, holding New Zealand up three times in-goal.

articles.title: McIlroy fades as Hatton leads in Dubai
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy's hopes of an eighth Race to Dubai title are dented as Tyrrell Hatton takes the outright lead into the fourth round of the DP World Tour Championship.
body: Rory McIlroy's hopes of winning a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title faded as he fell four shots behind leader Tyrrell Hatton after three rounds of the season-ending DP World Tour Championship.

Northern Irishman McIlroy started Saturday tied for the lead with Hatton but, while the Englishman remained at the top of the field with a four-under-par 68, McIlroy fell away with a 72 at the Earth Course in Dubai.
Hatton, on nine under for the tournament, holds a one-shot lead over France's Victor Perez as he bids for a first DP World Tour Championship, while Sweden's Mikael Lindberg is third on six under.
McIlroy is joint fourth in a group of four players which includes Spain's Eugenio Chacarra, the current leader in the Race to Dubai standings.

articles.title: McKenna to defend world title live on Sky Sports on December 4
articles.summary: Aaron McKenna will defend his middleweight world title on Friday December 4, live on Sky Sports.
body: IBF champion McKenna will fight unbeaten Latvian Jevgenijs Aleksejevs at The Venue in Riyadh in the main event of Riyadh Season Zuffa Boxing 14.
It will be McKenna's first defence of the world title belt he won by beating Etinosa Oliha on a memorable night in Dublin.
McKenna, 21-0 (10), who hails from Monaghan, Ireland, is a nine-year pro who vaulted into title contention with his April 2025 decision over former world champion Liam Smith.
While McKenna fought many times in Ireland as a top amateur, he returned home for the first time as a pro in August, capturing the world title with a one-sided victory over Oliha at Dublin's 3Arena.

articles.title: Magnificent Wales beat New Zealand for first time since 1953
articles.summary: Wales celebrate a first victory against New Zealand in 73 years with a brilliant 35-28 win to provide astonishing scenes in Cardiff.
body: Wales celebrated a first victory against New Zealand in 73 years with a brilliant performance to spark astonishing scenes in Cardiff.
Steve Tandy's unfancied side lifted a nation as they broke a 34-match losing sequence against the All Blacks that stretched back to 1953.

In a nine-try Nations Championship thriller at the Principality Stadium, Wales led 14-0, 21-7 and 35-21 before they held off New Zealand with a wonderful defensive display in the final quarter, led by flankers James Botham and Jac Morgan and lock Dafydd Jenkins.
The home side produced a stunning start with tries from inspirational scrum-half Tomos Williams and captain Dewi Lake inside the first six minutes.

articles.title: How FAA's ground stop impacts Saturday's college football schedule
articles.summary: The ground stop that halted air travel for a few hours Friday shook up Saturday's college football schedule, even resulting in a rare Sunday game. Locally, the most notable change is Rice pushing its kickoff against Tulane back from 1 p.m. to 3:30 p.m.
body: While No. 6 Texas had a delayed departure for its game at No. 21 LSU, that will still begin at 6:30 p.m. in Baton Rouge, La.
Texas A&M is at home against No. 8 Tennessee and will still kick off at 2 p.m. after the Volunteers traveled to College Station late Friday.

Baylor's game at No. 10 BYU was pushed back to a 6 p.m. start in Provo, Utah. It was originally scheduled for 2:30 p.m. The game could not be rescheduled to Sunday because BYU is not allowed to play on Sundays due to religious observances by The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, which runs the school.
The University of Houston was not impacted as the Cougars played Friday night and lost at Colorado.

articles.summary: Back Kirk Cousins in his return to Minnesota, take the points with New England against Detroit and expect points in an AFC East shootout at MetLife
body: The NFC South is tied up, like a bunch of two-wheeled farm tractors limping towards a home playoff game. The NFC North is maybe the best division ever (the numbers back it up!) and will be a thrill to watch at the close, especially with the arms race building up either through trades ( Kirk Cousins back to the Vikings, Jeffery Simmons to the Bears ) or defensive players returning ( Lions and Packers ).

The NFC West has a compelling three-team battle of attrition for first place while the Broncos/Chiefs AFC West showdown for an extremely important home-field slot (and maybe more?) should be wildly entertaining given the nature of those two teams. Same with the Bills and Patriots in the AFC East, although Buffalo holds an advantage there.

The AFC North is still anyone's game. Really, the only thing we know right now is the Jaguars look like a lock to win the AFC South. And they pressed their advantage, pushing their chips in for home field and a Super Bowl run.
